mail.intro: Where Quality Data sends mail from: Office 365 via Microsoft Graph or any SMTP server.
mail.offHelp: When off, Quality Data sends nothing: neither its notices nor the license's.
mail.displayNameHelp: Optional. What shows as the sender in the inbox, for example «Data quality».
mail.tenantIdHelp: In the Azure portal: Microsoft Entra ID → Overview → Tenant ID.
mail.clientIdHelp: The app registration in Entra ID → Overview → Application (client) ID. The app needs the Mail.Send application permission, with admin consent.
mail.clientSecretHelp: App registration → Certificates & secrets. Copy the Value (not the secret ID) when you create it: it is not shown again. Note when it expires.
mail.serverHelp: The SMTP server name, for example smtp.office365.com or the company's internal relay.
mail.encryptionHelp: STARTTLS goes with port 587 and direct TLS with 465. «None» only for a trusted internal relay (port 25).
mail.usernamePlaceholder: Empty for a relay without authentication.
mail.usernameHelp: Usually the mailbox's full address. In Office 365 over SMTP, the mailbox needs SMTP authentication enabled.
mail.passwordHelp: Stored encrypted and never shown again; leave the field empty to keep the saved one. With two-step verification, use an app password.
mail.resetLinkHelp: How long the link emailed by «Forgot your password?» works, between 5 minutes and one day. It works once and asking for another cancels the previous one. Local accounts only: directory accounts change it in LDAP / Active Directory.
mail.appRegistrationsPath: Entra ID → App registrations → New registration
mail.createApp: , create a single-tenant application (no redirect URL).
mail.createSecret: , create a client secret and copy its
mail.notTheId: (not the ID). Note when it expires.
mail.restrictRecommended: Recommended: restrict the app to the sender mailbox with an
mail.withoutRestriction: ); without it the app can send as any mailbox in the tenant.
mail.usesForm: Uses what is in the form, even if it is not saved.
mail.senderMailboxHelp: It must exist in the tenant. To restrict the app to this mailbox, use an application access policy in Exchange Online.
mail.senderAddressHelp: The address recipients will see. Many servers require it to match the user you authenticate with.
mail.senderMailboxNote: A mailbox (or shared mailbox) in the tenant: mail is sent as it.
mail.testSent: Sent to {{testTo}}. Check the inbox (and the spam folder).
mail.noOwnServer: This installation has no mail server of its own: configure your company's. Without it, no notices or license alerts are sent, nor account activation and password recovery emails.
mail.alertLanguageTip: The language of alert emails (failures, servers without communication, resources, changes on the machine). They also go to people without an account, so the company sets it.

ldap.intro: Sign in with corporate directory accounts. Local accounts keep working.
ldap.offHelp: When off, only local accounts can sign in (like the emergency administrator). Sessions already open are not closed.
ldap.serverUrlHelp: The domain controller. Use ldaps:// (port 636) to encrypt the connection; with ldap:// (389) turn on StartTLS. With several controllers, use the domain's DNS name (company.local).
ldap.starttlsHelp: Encrypts an ldap:// connection before sending passwords. Not used with ldaps://, which is already encrypted.
ldap.insecureHelp: Accepts any certificate, even a fake one: someone on the network could read the passwords. Testing only; in production the Quality Data server must trust the CA that signed the controller's certificate.
ldap.timeoutHelp: How long to wait for the directory before giving up. If it does not answer, sign-in says the directory is not responding instead of blaming the password. 5 seconds is usually enough.
ldap.passwordHelp: The service account's password. Stored encrypted and never shown again; leave the field empty to keep the saved one. If it expires, nobody from the directory can sign in: set it to never expire.
ldap.searchBaseHelp: Where people are searched from, including subfolders. The domain root (DC=company,DC=local) finds everyone; an OU (OU=Users,DC=…) narrows the search.
ldap.adminGroupsHelp: Copy the DN exactly as shown by «Test» (the person's groups). Only direct groups count, not nested ones. Changes apply at each person's next sign-in.
ldap.adminGroupsNote: One group DN per line. Its members are global administrators; for now only they sign in with the directory.
ldap.enable: Allow signing in with directory accounts
ldap.insecure: Do not verify the certificate (testing only)
ldap.serviceAccountHelp: An account with read access to the directory, used to look each person up before verifying their password.
ldap.bindDnHelp: The service account's full name. In AD you see it in its properties → Attribute Editor →
ldap.regularUserEnough: . A regular user without privileges is enough.
ldap.userFilterHelp: How the person signing in is found. The AD one searches by UPN or email. To require a group, add
ldap.placeholderNote: is replaced by what the person types in the email field when signing in. It must match exactly one entry.
ldap.usesForm: Uses what is in the form, even if it is not saved. It connects with the service account and, if you enter a user, looks them up and shows their groups. It does not verify any user password.
ldap.name: Name
ldap.switchedToEnv: Switched back to the environment variables.
ldap.savedOn: Saved. LDAP sign-in now uses these settings.
ldap.userNotFound: Connection OK, but the filter did not find that user.
ldap.noMail: — (no mail or userPrincipalName: cannot sign in)

oauth.title: OAuth2 / OIDC sign-in
oauth.intro: “Sign in with…” buttons on the sign-in page. People get in if they already have an account with that email (when the provider vouches for it) or linked their account under Settings → Linked accounts.
oauth.nameHelp: A short name, like «microsoft» or «google». If you change it later, update the redirect URL at the provider.
oauth.slugHelp: Lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens. It is the button text and goes in the redirect URL.
oauth.redirectUrl: Redirect URL (register it at the provider)
oauth.redirectUrlHelp: Copy it as is into the provider. In Entra ID: app registration → Authentication → Web → Redirect URI. In Google: OAuth credentials → Authorized redirect URIs.
oauth.clientIdHelp: The identifier of the application you created at the provider (in Entra ID, the Application ID).
oauth.clientSecretHelp: Stored encrypted and never shown again; leave the field empty to keep the saved one. When it expires at the provider, the button stops working.
oauth.microsoftHttpsLoginMicrosoftonline: Microsoft: https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant id>/v2.0. Google: https://accounts.google.com. With it, «Discover» fills in the three endpoints.
oauth.scopesHelp: What is requested from the provider. «openid email» is enough: Quality Data only needs the email, and people get in only if they already have an account with that email.
oauth.tenantIdRequired: Enter the Entra ID tenant ID to add Microsoft.
oauth.switchedToEnv: Switched back to the environment variables.
oauth.savedProviders_one: Saved. {{count}} provider active on the sign-in page.
oauth.savedProviders_other: Saved. {{count}} providers active on the sign-in page.
oauth.trustEmailTip: Links by email even when the provider does not say it is verified (Entra ID does not). Adding Microsoft with the company’s tenant id turns it on: that tenant only hands out the company’s addresses. Turn it off with a shared tenant (common, organizations). When off, each person links their account once under Settings → Linked accounts.

account.title: My account
account.subtitle: Your details in this installation and the accounts you sign in with.
account.noProviders: No sign-in provider is configured. An administrator turns it on under Settings → OAuth2 / OIDC.
account.linked: Done: your {{provider}} account is linked. From now on you can sign in with it.

errors.taken: That account is already linked to another user. Ask whoever has it to unlink it.
errors.failed: The account could not be linked: it was cancelled or the provider did not answer. Try again.
errors.load: Your linked accounts could not be read.

account.name: Name
account.photoHint: JPEG, PNG, WebP or GIF up to 256 KB. A photo you upload wins over Google's or another provider's; if you remove it, the provider's comes back when you sign in with it.
account.linkedSubtitle: The Google, Microsoft or other accounts you sign in to this one with. You can link one even if its email is not your user's.
account.photoTooBig: The photo is {{kb}} KB: the maximum is 256 KB. Shrink or crop it.

users.subtitle: Your company's accounts. Whoever you add here gets a link by email to choose their password; until then they cannot sign in.

users.name: Name (optional)

secrets.title: Global variables
secrets.subtitle: What is used in several places is registered once here: a database connection, an API key… Its value is stored encrypted and never shown again; when it changes, the new one is used from then on.
secrets.name: Name
secrets.nameHint: Letters, numbers, _ . - and starting with a letter or _.
secrets.invalidName: Letters, numbers, _ . - and starting with a letter or _ (as in KNIME).
secrets.confirmBody: {{name}} and its value will be deleted. This cannot be undone.

iam.nameHint: Lowercase letters, digits and -, up to 64; starts with a letter.

managed.quality-steward: Whoever owns the rules and pipelines: every quality action except seeing personal data.
managed.quality-analyst: Whoever investigates findings: sees everything, personal data included, runs pipelines and exports results.
managed.quality-viewer: Managers and dashboards: pipelines, results and rules, without personal data.
managed.auditor: Internal control: sees everything and the audit log, without personal data.

groups.title: Groups
groups.subtitle: Their people get their policies. They are added by hand or come from directory groups (LDAP / AD) at every sign-in.
groups.loadError: The groups could not be read.
groups.name: Name
groups.directoryHint: One DN per line: whoever is in that LDAP / AD group joins at sign-in.
groups.confirmBody: {{name}} is deleted; its people lose what its policies gave them.

policies.title: Policies
policies.subtitle: The built-in ones come with the application and do not change. Your own allow or deny actions on resources (*, secret/BD_*…); a deny always wins.
policies.loadError: The policies could not be read.
policies.name: Name
policies.resourcesHint: One per line: * (everything) or kind/name, with * as a wildcard: secret/BD_*, pipeline/cartera-*.
policies.confirmBody: {{name}} is deleted; whoever had it loses what it gave.

serviceAccounts.title: Service accounts
serviceAccounts.subtitle: Tokens for integrations and scripts: they call the API with «Authorization: Bearer <token>». Each belongs to whoever creates it and can do at most what they can.
serviceAccounts.loadError: The service accounts could not be read.
serviceAccounts.empty: There are no service accounts yet.
serviceAccounts.name: Name
serviceAccounts.policiesHint: With none, it has what you have; with some, only what both they and your permissions allow.
serviceAccounts.expiresHint: Optional. Without a date, it does not expire.
serviceAccounts.tokenOnce: This is the token: copy it now, it is not shown again.
serviceAccounts.deleted: Service account {{name}} deleted: its token stops working.
serviceAccounts.confirmBody: {{name}} is deleted and its token stops working at once.

machines.cardDesc: The machines that run the jobs: approve the new ones.
machines.title: Execution
machines.subtitle: The installation's machines. A new one joins pending and takes no work until it is approved here.
machines.loadError: The machines could not be read.
machines.noCa: This installation has no certificate authority yet: no machine can join.
machines.name: Machine

done.drain: {{name}} is draining: it finishes what it has and gets nothing new.
done.retire: {{name}} retired: its certificate is refused from now on.

machines.confirmBody: {{name}} is out for good: its certificate is refused and its sessions end. To come back it has to join again.

join.roleHint: For now worker and lake-replica have an installation command. For the other roles you get the token alone.
join.poolHint: Optional: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens.
join.drivesHint: Optional: the mounted path of each of its drives, one per line (each a filesystem of its own, mounted and empty); the command then carries them. Left empty, add --drive followed by each path to the command by hand.
join.once: Shown only this once: copy it now. Once this panel is closed it cannot be seen again; if it is lost, ask for a new one.
join.for: For one machine of role {{role}} in pool {{pool}}.
join.forNoPool: For one machine of role {{role}}, without a pool.
join.runAsRoot: Run it as root on the new server. It checks what it downloads, installs the machine and starts it; the machine then appears in this list as pending approval and takes no work until you approve it.
join.addDrives: No drives were given: before running it, add --drive followed by the path of each drive (each a filesystem of its own, mounted and empty) at the end of the command.
join.noCommand: There is no installation command for it: nothing installs the role {{role}} yet, or this installation's public address is not HTTPS. The token is what a machine's agent joins with; there is no procedure yet for using it by hand.

access.title: Users and access
access.subtitle: Who gets in and what they can do: each account gets policies directly or through its groups.

lake.cardDesc: The lake's servers: whether the main lake and the replica answer, and their admin keys.
lake.title: Lake
lake.subtitle: The lake's servers: the main lake and its replica. Whether each answers, and the keys of its admin user, which the application configures the replication with.

main.title: The main lake
main.intro: The application asks the main lake's admin API with the keys kept below, where it reaches the lake, presenting this installation's machine certificate. Nothing is changed on it.
main.loadError: The main lake's state could not be read.
main.noAddress: This installation reaches no lake (LAKE_ENDPOINT is not set): tell whoever supports your installation.
main.noKeys: The main lake is at {{endpoint}}: paste its admin keys below to reach it.
main.answered: The main lake answers with the kept keys: {{online}} drives online, {{offline}} offline.
main.keysRefused: The main lake refuses the kept keys ({{code}}): paste the ones shown when its stack was brought up.
main.unreachable: The main lake could not be reached at {{endpoint}}: {{detail}}

replica.title: The replica
replica.intro: The application asks the replica's admin API with the keys kept below, through its gate, presenting this installation's machine certificate. Nothing is changed on it.
replica.loadError: The replica's state could not be read.
replica.noMachine: No replica has joined yet: add a machine of role lake-replica in Settings → Execution.
replica.pending: {{machine}} joined and waits to be approved in Settings → Execution.
replica.several: More than one replica is approved ({{machines}}): retire the ones that are not the replica.
replica.noKeys: {{machine}} is the replica: paste its admin keys below to reach it.
replica.answered: {{machine}} answers with the kept keys: {{online}} drives online, {{offline}} offline.
replica.keysRefused: {{machine}} refuses the kept keys ({{code}}): paste the ones join.sh showed on it.

mainAdmin.title: The main lake's admin user
mainAdmin.intro: When the lake's stack was brought up, infra/rustfs/admin-user.sh made the platform's admin user and showed its access key and secret once, on that server's terminal. Paste both here: they are kept sealed and never shown again, here or anywhere.
mainAdmin.none: Not kept yet: paste the keys shown when the lake's stack was brought up.
mainAdmin.secretHint: The 64 hex digits shown once. It is not shown again after saving.
mainAdmin.saved: The main lake's admin keys are kept.

pool.title: The lake's pool
pool.intro: A lake grows by pools of at least four servers, each with its own drives. Define the pool main here before any of its servers is installed: its servers' names, in order, as DNS resolves them, and how many drives each has. Then copy each server's command, which names it, and run it on that server. The pool forms when all of them are up. Once a server has joined, the layout no longer changes.
pool.loadError: The lake's pool could not be read.
pool.nodesHint: One per line, in order: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, 4 to 16 servers. Each must resolve in DNS from the others.
pool.drivesHint: How many drives each server has: 1 to 16, the same on every server.
pool.defined: The pool main is saved. Ask each server's command below.
pool.nodeDrivesHint: The mounted paths of this server's drives, one per line, as many as the pool says; or leave it empty and add --drive and each path to the command by hand.

admin.title: The replica's admin user
admin.intro: When the replica's command started it, join.sh made the platform's admin user and showed its access key and secret once, on that server's terminal. Paste both here: they are kept sealed and never shown again, here or anywhere.
admin.none: Not kept yet: paste the keys join.sh showed on the replica.
admin.kept: Kept: {{access}}, pasted on {{at}}. Paste them again to replace them.
admin.loadError: What is kept could not be read.
admin.secretHint: The 64 hex digits join.sh showed once. It is not shown again after saving.
admin.saved: The replica's admin keys are kept.

replication.title: The replication
replication.intro: The application makes every company's warehouse on the main lake when it is missing, and configures the main lake to copy it into the replica, where each object is kept {{days}} days in COMPLIANCE mode, which no one can shorten or delete; the main lake's old versions are removed after {{noncurrent}} days. It runs when keys are kept and every hour, and changes nothing when all is in place.
replication.loadError: The replication's state could not be read.
replication.noAddress: This installation reaches no main lake: tell whoever supports your installation.
replication.noReplica: No single replica is approved: see The replica.
replication.noKeysMain: The main lake's admin keys are not kept yet.
replication.noKeysReplica: The replica's admin keys are not kept yet.
replication.none: No warehouse has been configured yet.
replication.noWarehouse: Not on the main lake yet
replication.made: Made on the main lake; its replication waits for the replica and its keys

platform.title: Platform
platform.intro: What the whole installation shares. Changes apply on save.
platform.readError: Could not read the platform settings.
platform.timezoneHelp: The installation's time: the automatic update window is read in it, and new schedules take it when they do not name another. Schedules already saved keep their own.
platform.timezoneHint: An IANA name, such as America/Bogota, Europe/Madrid or UTC.
